## Cluster A: Data-Centric and Loss-Based Methods

Methods that modify which samples contribute or how much each sample's loss matters.

<details>
<summary><strong>SFT — Standard Fine-Tuning</strong></summary>

- **What**: Vanilla cross-entropy on all training samples equally
- **Why insufficient**: Does not distinguish shortcut from genuine reasoning samples; shortcuts dominate gradients
- **Performance**: 68.8% accuracy, 19.4% robustness (baseline)

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Data Filtering — Remove high-confidence samples</strong></summary>

- **What**: Train a warmup model, remove samples with high confidence (>0.90), retrain on filtered data
- **Why insufficient**: Shortcut samples are correctly labeled — confidence-based filtering has high variance across tasks
- **Performance**: 74.7% accuracy, 54.6% robustness — but collapses on Financial (68.4% rob) while failing on Math (26.6% rob)

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>JTT — Just Train Twice</strong></summary>

- **What**: Warmup, identify misclassified samples, upsample them, retrain
- **Why insufficient**: Shortcut samples are correctly classified during warmup; JTT upsamples the wrong subset
- **Performance**: 67.9% accuracy, 19.0% robustness — near SFT baseline

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Focal Loss</strong></summary>

- **What**: $(1 - p_t)^\gamma$ modulated cross-entropy — downweights easy (high-confidence) samples
- **Why insufficient**: Shortcuts produce high confidence but are not "easy" in the generalisation sense
- **Performance**: 68.2% accuracy, 18.2% robustness

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Influence Filtering</strong></summary>

- **What**: Compute influence functions to identify harmful training samples, remove them
- **Why insufficient**: Discards training data entirely; exhibits extreme cross-task variance (83.2% on Causal, 63.4% on Financial)
- **Performance**: 76.0% accuracy, 47.7% robustness — best non-SART method overall

</details>

---

## Cluster B: Distributionally Robust and Invariant Methods

Methods that optimise worst-case or invariant objectives across groups/environments.

<details>
<summary><strong>Group DRO — Distributionally Robust Optimization</strong></summary>

- **What**: Worst-group optimization using exponentiated gradient on group weights
- **Why insufficient**: Requires explicit group annotations (shortcut vs. non-shortcut labels) unavailable in practice
- **Performance**: 73.5% accuracy, 36.0% robustness

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>IRM — Invariant Risk Minimization</strong></summary>

- **What**: Penalise gradient-based invariance violation across environments
- **Why insufficient**: Requires multiple training environments; gradient penalty is insufficient to remove shortcut directions
- **Performance**: 73.3% accuracy, 34.4% robustness

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>V-REx — Variance of Risks Extrapolation</strong></summary>

- **What**: Penalise variance of per-environment risks
- **Why insufficient**: Same environment requirement as IRM; moderate gains
- **Performance**: 72.1% accuracy, 34.9% robustness

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Fishr — Gradient Variance Equalization</strong></summary>

- **What**: Match gradient variances across groups via EMA
- **Why insufficient**: Equalizing variance does not correct gradient direction; fails to detect which variance is harmful
- **Performance**: 68.1% accuracy, 16.7% robustness — worse than SFT on robustness

</details>

---

## Cluster C: Debiasing and Meta-Learning Methods

Methods that learn from model failures or use meta-objectives.

<details>
<summary><strong>LfF — Learning from Failure</strong></summary>

- **What**: Train a biased model and a debiased model simultaneously; reweight based on biased model's mistakes
- **Why insufficient**: The biased model may not align with the actual shortcut in reasoning tasks
- **Performance**: 69.0% accuracy, 19.4% robustness

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Self-Consistency Decoding</strong></summary>

- **What**: Sample multiple reasoning paths at inference, take majority vote
- **Why insufficient**: Operates at inference time only — shortcut patterns remain encoded in model parameters
- **Performance**: 69.1% accuracy, 23.3% robustness

</details>

---

## Gap Synthesis

| Gap | Consequence | SART Contribution |
|-----|-------------|-------------------|
| No method detects shortcuts from gradient structure | Shortcut samples invisible to label/loss-based filters | ShortcutScore: gradient alignment + answer concentration |
| No method corrects gradient directions during training | Even downweighted shortcuts inject harmful gradient components | Gradient Surgery: projection + suppression |
| Methods require group annotations or multiple environments | Impractical for real-world reasoning tasks | SART is annotation-free and single-environment |
